etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Late Latin ovalis, from ovum; cognate with French and Italian ovale, Dutch ovaal. From 1570.

definitions.definition: An elongated round shape resembling an egg or ellipse.
A thing having such a shape, such as an arena.
(mathematics) In a projective plane, a set of points such that no three are collinear and there is a unique tangent line at each point.
(Australia) A sports field, typically but not exclusively oval in shape.
Having the shape of an oval.
Of or pertaining to an ovum.

quote.text: Every congenital abnormality is doubtless due to a peculiarity in the sperm or oval elements or in their mingling, or to some disturbance in their early development.
